subject: general
question: Preventive detention is part of which Article in the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 22**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 22** of the Indian Constitution deals with **preventive detention and the rights of individuals who are detained**.
 
• Under this article, certain safeguards are provided to individuals who are arrested or detained, including the right to be informed of the grounds of arrest and the right to consult and be defended by a legal practitioner of their choice.
 
• Article 22 also includes provisions for the establishment of advisory boards to review cases of preventive detention.
 
• The article ensures that no person can be detained for more than three months without the recommendation of an advisory board.
 
• Preventive detention is a measure to prevent individuals from committing future crimes or acting in a manner that could threaten public order or national security.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Seventh Schedule **of the Constitution contains three lists which delineate the subjects under the **Union, State, and Concurrent lists**.
 
• Amendments to the Constitution can be made through a process outlined in **Article 368**.
